title: Annotatio IV §.IX open: Fifth century — Chrysostom and Augustine as chief witnesses
pass_a_gloss: §. IX. The Testimonies of the FIFTH age — or the last of those to which it was given to glory in the purer Evangelical doctrine — although most abundant ones could be gathered and brought from more Fathers both Greek and Latin, Theodoret, Cyril, Prosper of Aquitaine, Fulgentius and others, yet it will suffice us in this place to have rested in the Sentences of two Fathers who easily snatch the palm of both broader learning and sacred Commentary and eloquence from Predecessors and Successors. One of these the Doctor par excellence of the Eastern, the other of the Western Church, and common, both deserves to be called and is commonly wont to be called — I mean S. CHRYSOSTOM and S. AUGUSTINE.
pass_b_english: §.IX: for the FIFTH century — last of the purer Evangelical ages — many Fathers could be cited, but two snatch the palm.
East and West’s doctors par excellence: Chrysostom and Augustine.
source_text: §. IX. Testimonia SECULI QUINTI, seu postremi eorum, quibus de puriori doctrina Evangelica gloriari datum est, etsi ex pluribus Patribus tàm Græcis, quam Latinis, Theodoreto, Cyrillo, Prospero Aquitanico, Fulgentio aliisque colligi adducique possent uberrima, nobis tamen hôc locô suffecerit in duorum, diffusioris cùm eruditionis, tùm Commentationis atque eloquii sacri, palmam, & Antecessoribus, & Successoribus, facilè præripientium Patrum Sententiis acquievisse. Alter horum Orientalis, Occidentalis Ecclesiæ alter Doctor kat' exochēn communisque & meretur dici, & vulgò consuevit appellari, S. CHRYSOSTOMUM intelligo, & S. AUGUSTINUM.
